operations.description: Get an Enterprise File Storage service
operations.longDescription: Returns the service, including its region, performance level, quota and status.

operations.description: Update an Enterprise File Storage service
operations.longDescription: Updates the service name, the only property that can be changed. The change applies immediately, whatever the service status.
Starts the change of the admin, tech or billing contact and returns the request IDs.
Confirms the termination with the emailed token and records your reason.
Returns a new token and the endpoint used to query the service metrics. Each call creates a new token, valid until the returned expiry date.

parameters.name: detail
parameters.description: Get detailed information about each network

operations.longDescription: Returns the networks of the service, with only their IDs unless `detail` is true. A service on the public network has no network, so the list is empty.

Returns the network status and the URN of the vRack Services it is attached to. The status moves to associated only after an endpoint is created on the vRack Services, and share access paths are returned only in that status.
Returns the product offers this service can change to (upgrade or downgrade), including plan code, quota, performance level, and the constraints that apply to the change.
Returns contacts, creation and expiration dates, and renewal settings.
Changes how the service renews; `renew` is the only editable field.

parameters.name: detail
parameters.description: Get detailed information about each share

parameters.name: mountPointName
parameters.description: If specified, returns only shares with given mount point name

operations.longDescription: Returns the ID and name of each share of the service. Set `detail` to true to get all share properties.

Creates an NFS share, empty or from a manual snapshot, in which case the share must be at least the size of the snapshot. Creation is asynchronous: the share is returned with status creating, follow its status until available. The total size of the shares cannot exceed the service capacity.
Permanently deletes the share and its ACLs. Deletion is asynchronous. Delete the snapshots and replications of the share first.
Returns the share properties, its status and its access mode. To get the paths used to mount the share, list its access paths.
Updates the share name and description. To change the size, use *Extend a share* or *Shrink a share*.
Returns the paths used to mount the share, with the preferred one first. The list stays empty until the network status of the service is associated.
Returns the path used to mount the share. The preferred path goes through the storage node that hosts the share.
Returns the ACLs of the share, including those still being applied or removed. Check the status of each ACL to know whether it is in effect.

Grants an IPv4 address or IPv4 CIDR block read-only or read-write access to the share. Creation is asynchronous: the ACL is returned with status queued_to_apply, follow its status until active. The call is rejected while the share is being created, resized, reverted or replicated.
Revokes access to the share. Clients already mounting the share using it lose access. Deletion is asynchronous: the ACL stays listed with status queued_to_deny or denying until it is removed.
Returns the ACL and its status. An ACL in error is not applied to the share: delete it and create it again.

Increases the share to the given size in GB, which must be greater than its current size. The share must be available, and the change is asynchronous: its status moves to extending, then back to available, or to extending_error if it fails.

operations.description: Revert a share to its latest snapshot
operations.longDescription: Restores the share content to the given snapshot, which must be the most recent snapshot of the share. Data written after this snapshot is permanently lost. The share and the snapshot must be available, and the revert is asynchronous: follow the share status until it is available, or reverting_error if it fails.

apis.description: Revert a share to it's latest snapshot

operations.longDescription: Reduces the share to the given size in GB, which must be smaller than its current size. The share must be available, and the change is asynchronous: follow the share status until it is available again. If the new size is smaller than the space already used, the share keeps its current size.

parameters.name: detail
parameters.description: Get detailed information about each snapshot

operations.longDescription: Returns the ID and name of each snapshot of the share, including the snapshots taken automatically and by the system. Set `detail` to true to get all snapshot properties, such as their type and status.
Creates a manual snapshot of the share. Creation is asynchronous: the snapshot is returned with status creating, follow its status until available. The share must be in status available.

Permanently deletes the snapshot. Deletion is asynchronous: follow the snapshot until it no longer exists. System snapshots cannot be deleted, and a manual snapshot must be in status available or error.
Returns the snapshot properties, its status and its type: manual, automatic when taken by the snapshot policy, or system. Holding an automatic snapshot turns it into a manual snapshot with a new ID.
Updates the snapshot name and description. Only manual snapshots can be updated: hold an automatic snapshot first.

Converts an automatic snapshot into a manual snapshot with a new ID, which the snapshot policy no longer deletes. Holding is asynchronous: follow the status of the returned snapshot until it is available. A held snapshot will not be released and is kept until you delete it.
Returns the snapshot policy applied to the share and the status of its assignment. A share that was never assigned a policy uses the default snapshot policy of the service.

Applies one of the snapshot policies of the service to the share. The share and the policy must be available, and the default policy cannot be assigned, so a share cannot be moved back to it. The update is asynchronous: follow the snapshot policy status of the share until active.
Returns the percentage of the share size reserved for snapshots and the status of its last update.

Changes the percentage of the share size reserved for snapshots without changing the share size, so a higher reserve leaves less space for data. The share must be available. The update is asynchronous: follow the snapshot reserve status until it returns to active.
Returns the share replications of the service, whether this service is the source or the destination.

Creates a share replication from a share of this service to the service given in `destinationServiceId`. It is returned with status pending, and the replication only starts after it is accepted on the destination service. To find a compatible destination, use *List compatible replication destinations*.

Deletes the share replication. Deletion is asynchronous and blocked while the replication is in status cutting_over, deleting or error. If the replication was accepted, the destination share is deleted with it.
Returns the source, destination, status and progress of the replication, in percent.

Accepts the share replication and creates the destination share on this service, with the name, size and protocol given in the body. The replication must be in status pending. Acceptance is asynchronous: the replication is returned with status accepted, follow its progress until the replica state is in_sync.

Cuts over the share replication: the destination share becomes the primary, the replication stops, and the source and destination data diverge after it, so the operation cannot be undone. The call must be made on the destination service, and the replication must be in status accepted. The cutover is asynchronous: follow the status of the share replication until it is completed.

parameters.name: compatibleOnly
parameters.description: If set to true, only services compatible as share replication destinations for the given source are returned

operations.longDescription: Returns, for each service on which you are allowed to accept share replications, whether it can be a destination for share replications from this service, and the reason when it cannot. A destination is compatible when it is in the same region as the source service, and when the source service uses a public network while the destination uses a vRack network. Set `compatibleOnly` to true to return only compatible destinations.

iamActions.name: storageNetApp:apiovh:shareReplication/accept
iamActions.description: Needed on a destination EFS service for it to be listed in the response body

operations.longDescription: Returns the snapshot policies, including the default one. Each item contains only the policy ID and name: get a snapshot policy to read its rules and status.

Creates a policy made of rules, each with a schedule, a snapshot name prefix and a number of copies to keep. Creation is asynchronous: follow the snapshot policy status until it is available. The policy takes effect only once it is assigned to a share.

Deletes the snapshot policy and its schedules. A policy applied to a share cannot be deleted: apply another non-default policy to the share first. The default policy cannot be deleted, and deletion is asynchronous: follow the snapshot policy status until the policy is no longer found.
Returns the snapshot policy with its rules and status. A policy can be updated, deleted or assigned to a share only when its status is available.
Updates the policy name and description. Rules cannot be changed: create a new policy instead. The policy must be available, and the default policy cannot be updated.

operations.description: Ask for the termination of your service
operations.longDescription: Emails a termination token to the admin contact, to use with *Confirm service termination*.
